topic: Write your first test for your project: what a unit test is, one test for one function, run it in the terminal, test the edge case, and run tests before every push (JavaScript + Jest)
save_reason: A 5-step 'first test' cheat sheet (install, name the file, one test per function, test the edge case, run before you push) on slide 7, with the full example test in the caption.
send_reason: Send this to a friend whose project breaks every time they change something.

cover.concept: Surreal landscape: a vast white salt flat at dawn with a long straight row of tall glowing lanterns running to the horizon, one tiny figure walking along the row with a small torch, checking each lantern.
hooks: This is how real teams know their code works. (curiosity)
Write your first test in 20 minutes. (confidence)
Your first project can have real tests. (ambition)
One test file can catch bugs before anyone sees them. (awe)
cover.hookDraft: This is how real teams know their code works.
cover.lineDraft: Write your first test this week, in first year.

slides.label: Save this
slides.idea: Results first + save promise: a terminal where every test passes in green.
slides.title: This is what passing tests look like.
slides.line: Save this and add tests to your project.
slides.screen: Terminal cropped big: `npm test` output for a fictional notes app (aarav-codes/notes-app) with 4 passing tests and the 'Tests: 4 passed' summary (.focus)

slides.label: Myth
slides.idea: Break a belief: tests are not only for big companies; a test is a few lines that check one function.
slides.title: A test is just a few lines of code.
slides.line: It runs your function and checks the answer.
slides.screen: Code editor cropped big: notes.test.js with one short test calling countWords("hello world") and expecting 2 (.focus on the expect line)

slides.label: Better way
slides.idea: Re-hook: instead of clicking through the app after every change, run one command.
slides.title: Here's a faster way: run one command.
slides.line: npm test checks all your tests in one go.
slides.screen: Terminal cropped big: `npm test` running, showing the test file names with ticks

slides.label: Before you code
slides.idea: Write down the tricky inputs first (empty, very long, wrong type) on paper.
slides.title: Write down the tricky inputs first.
slides.line: Then write one test for each of them.

slides.label: Edge cases
slides.idea: Won't work unless you test the edge case too, e.g. empty text returns 0.
slides.title: This won't work unless you test the edge cases.
slides.line: Check what happens with empty text, not just normal text.
slides.screen: Test output cropped big: one failing test 'returns 0 for empty text' in red with expected 0 / received 1 (.focus), then the fixed run passing

slides.label: Screenshot this
slides.idea: Cheat sheet: the 5 steps to your first test.
slides.title: Here's the easy way: follow these 5 steps.
slides.line: Screenshot this before you start your next feature.
slides.screen: A README-style checklist (.md) 'My first test': install Jest, name the file .test.js, one test per function, test the edge case, run npm test before git push
